category: C · Weak, variational, conservative, integral, and discrete physics

formulations.name: Weak residual statement
formulations.category: C · Weak, variational, conservative, integral, and discrete physics
formulations.meaning: Tests the governing residual against admissible test functions instead of demanding pointwise equality.
formulations.purpose: Reduces dependence on pointwise strong-form enforcement.
formulations.relation: It changes the mathematical norm/test space in which physics is enforced.
formulations.symbols: \(v\): test function; \(V\): test space; \(R_v\): weak residual functional.

formulations.name: Integration-by-parts weak form (elliptic example)
formulations.category: C · Weak, variational, conservative, integral, and discrete physics
formulations.meaning: Shows integration by parts for a representative second-order divergence-form elliptic operator, transferring one derivative from the trial field to the test function and exposing the natural boundary term.
formulations.purpose: Illustrates how weak formulations can lower trial-function derivative requirements and treat natural boundary data explicitly.
formulations.relation: The exact signs, coefficients, and boundary terms are operator-dependent; this displayed identity is an elliptic example rather than a universal integration-by-parts template.
formulations.symbols: \(A\): scalar/tensor diffusion or constitutive coefficient; \(v\): test function; \(\mathbf{n}\): outward unit normal.

formulations.name: Galerkin/quadrature weak loss
formulations.category: C · Weak, variational, conservative, integral, and discrete physics
formulations.meaning: Approximates weak residual integrals with quadrature and multiple test functions.
formulations.purpose: Makes test-space and quadrature choices explicit trainable/numerical design variables.
formulations.relation: It is the discrete optimization counterpart of the continuous weak statement.
formulations.symbols: \(N_v\): number of test functions; \(N_q\): quadrature points; \(w_q\): quadrature weights including any required geometric/Jacobian factors.

formulations.name: Variational stationarity and energy minimum
formulations.category: C · Weak, variational, conservative, integral, and discrete physics
formulations.equation: \delta\Pi[u^\star;v]=0\quad\forall v\in V_0,\qquad u_{\theta^\star}\approx u^\star,\qquad \text{and, when }\Pi\text{ admits a minimum principle,}\quad \theta^\star=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\theta}\Pi[u_\theta]
formulations.meaning: States the exact variational problem in function space as stationarity of the physical functional and then distinguishes the neural approximation from that exact target; minimization is valid only when the problem admits a minimum principle.
formulations.purpose: Avoids both treating every variational formulation as an energy minimum and implying that a finite neural trial space satisfies the exact Euler–Lagrange stationarity condition for every admissible variation.
formulations.relation: For general stationary or saddle formulations the neural method seeks an approximate stationary solution in its trial class; for suitable coercive/minimum-principle problems the common Ritz form minimizes \(\Pi[u_\theta]\).
formulations.symbols: \(u^\star\): exact variational solution; \(\Pi\): problem-specific variational/energy functional; \(\delta\Pi[u;v]\): first variation in admissible direction \(v\); \(V_0\): admissible variation/test space.

formulations.name: Total potential-energy objective
formulations.category: C · Weak, variational, conservative, integral, and discrete physics
formulations.meaning: Combines internal strain energy, external work, and—when a conservative or penalty-potential representation exists—a contact contribution.
formulations.relation: It is a concrete minimum/stationary-energy specialization of F031; nonconservative contact/friction laws may require inequality, complementarity, or other residual formulations rather than a scalar contact potential.
formulations.symbols: \(U\): internal energy; \(W_{ext}\): external work; \(\Pi_{contact}\): contact potential/penalty contribution when defined.

formulations.name: Entropy admissibility inequality
formulations.category: C · Weak, variational, conservative, integral, and discrete physics
formulations.meaning: Adds an entropy condition to select the physically admissible weak solution of a conservation law.
formulations.purpose: Addresses non-uniqueness and shock admissibility that a small strong residual alone may not resolve.
formulations.relation: It supplements the governing conservation law with a physically meaningful inequality under the displayed entropy-pair sign convention.
formulations.symbols: \(\eta\): convex entropy function; \(\mathbf{q}_\eta\): corresponding entropy flux.

formulations.name: Entropy-violation penalty
formulations.category: C · Weak, variational, conservative, integral, and discrete physics
formulations.meaning: Penalizes violation of an entropy inequality at training points.
formulations.purpose: Turns admissibility into a differentiable training signal.
formulations.relation: It is an extended loss term rather than a replacement for the conservation residual.
formulations.symbols: \(\max(0,\cdot)\): positive-part operator selecting only inequality violations.

formulations.name: Integral conservation balance
formulations.category: C · Weak, variational, conservative, integral, and discrete physics
formulations.meaning: Expresses a scalar conservation law over a finite control volume.
formulations.purpose: Provides a physically integral criterion that does not rely solely on pointwise differential residuals.
formulations.relation: Vector systems use the corresponding componentwise/vector balance; this form motivates conservative PINNs and conservation-aware validation.
formulations.symbols: \(V\): control volume; \(\mathbf{F}\): physical flux; \(s\): source; \(\mathbf{n}\): outward unit normal.

formulations.name: Finite-volume residual
formulations.category: C · Weak, variational, conservative, integral, and discrete physics
formulations.meaning: Represents a discrete local conservation balance using cell volume and face-integrated numerical flux contributions.
formulations.purpose: Preserves flux-oriented numerical structure inside a physics-informed loss.
formulations.relation: It is a first-order implicit time-update example; other finite-volume time integrators alter the temporal and flux evaluation levels while preserving the local balance structure.
formulations.symbols: \(V_i\): cell/control volume; \(\Gamma_{i,f}\): face \(f\) with measure \(|\Gamma_{i,f}|\); \(\widehat{F}_{i,f}\): outward-normal numerical flux density through the face; \(\Delta t\): time step.

formulations.name: Finite-difference residual
formulations.category: C · Weak, variational, conservative, integral, and discrete physics
formulations.meaning: Applies a discrete finite-difference approximation of the governing operator to network predictions.
formulations.purpose: Provides a grid-based alternative to continuous AD residuals.
formulations.relation: It reintroduces a discretization scale \(h\) while retaining trainable physics enforcement.

formulations.name: Convolutional discrete-operator residual
formulations.category: C · Weak, variational, conservative, integral, and discrete physics
formulations.meaning: Uses convolution kernels as discrete derivative/physics operators on grid-like outputs.
formulations.purpose: Efficiently enforces local numerical relations in convolutional physics-informed models.
formulations.relation: It shifts differential evaluation from coordinate AD to structured filtering.

formulations.name: Boundary-integral representation (Laplace-type)
formulations.category: C · Weak, variational, conservative, integral, and discrete physics
formulations.meaning: Gives a Green-representation boundary integral for a Laplace-type homogeneous interior equation, using a fundamental solution convention satisfying \(-\Delta_{\mathbf y}G(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})=\delta(\mathbf{x}-\mathbf{y})\).
formulations.purpose: Moves the representation of suitable elliptic physics from the domain to boundary quantities.
formulations.relation: The coefficient \(c(\mathbf{x})\), sign convention, conormal derivative, and any domain/source integral depend on the governing operator and whether \(\mathbf{x}\) lies in the interior or on the boundary; this is not a universal PDE identity.
formulations.symbols: \(G\): chosen fundamental/Green solution; \(q_\theta=\partial_nu_\theta\): outward normal derivative for the displayed Laplace convention; \(c(\mathbf{x})\): geometry/location-dependent coefficient.

formulations.name: Fredholm-type integral-equation residual
formulations.category: C · Weak, variational, conservative, integral, and discrete physics
formulations.meaning: Defines a representative second-kind Fredholm-type physics residual through an integral operator rather than a local differential operator.
formulations.purpose: Supports nonlocal and integral-equation physics while avoiding the implication that every integral equation has this exact second-kind structure.
formulations.relation: First-kind, nonlinear, boundary-integral, Volterra, and other integral equations require their corresponding operator form.

formulations.name: Fractional/nonlocal residual
formulations.category: C · Weak, variational, conservative, integral, and discrete physics
formulations.meaning: Includes a Caputo fractional derivative in the governing residual.
formulations.purpose: Extends physics-informed learning to memory and nonlocal evolution.
formulations.relation: This displayed time-fractional form is representative; space-fractional and other definitions use their corresponding nonlocal operators and often combine AD for integer derivatives with numerical treatment of the fractional term.
formulations.symbols: \({}^{C}D_t^\alpha\): Caputo-type fractional derivative of order \(\alpha\); \(\mathcal{N}\): remaining operator.

formulations.name: Coupled automatic–numerical differentiation
formulations.category: C · Weak, variational, conservative, integral, and discrete physics
formulations.meaning: Combines derivatives computed by automatic and numerical differentiation inside one residual.
formulations.purpose: Trades off continuous differentiability, cost, accuracy, and numerical structure.
formulations.relation: It modifies the residual-evaluation pathway without changing the governing physics.
formulations.symbols: \(D_{AD}\), \(D_{ND}\): derivative operators evaluated by automatic and numerical differentiation.
